meta_description: Digital thread for machining traceability on a permissioned ledger — audit preparation down 80% and full part provenance in one query

blocks.x: Digital thread for machining traceability on a permissioned ledger — audit preparation down 80% and full part provenance in one query

Identity withheld — an aerospace supplier whose traceability lived in filing cabinets and whose customer audits started with a letter and ended three weeks later. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline audit costed the cabinets: 19 person-days to assemble one part's full provenance, three findings on record-retrieval timeliness in two years, and a customer demanding digital thread evidence for its next program.
Traceability data existed — machine logs, CMM results, material certs — but in systems that didn't know each other. Assembling the thread was archaeology, and archaeology doesn't scale to every part.

We anchored the digital thread on a permissioned ledger: material certs, machine events, inspection results and sign-offs hashed and linked per serial from melt to ship, the ledger shared read-only with customers under contract, and provenance queries returning the full chain in seconds. The filing cabinets became the archive, not the system.
